# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 7 LUTs, 9 FFs, WNS 0.553 ns and WHS 0.135 ns. Iteration 1 passed simulation and timing but used 10 LUTs, so it failed the minimize-LUTs objective; its 8-bit counter with natural wrap is the pattern to avoid repeating. The current top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Using an 8-bit counter with an explicit terminal-count clear may let Vivado share the wrap detection with the counter’s reset logic and reduce LUT use while preserving the incumbent’s 8-bit phase sequence.

## Instruction for generator
Change the 32-bit `counter` to 8 bits and keep an explicit `if (counter == 8'hFF) counter <= 8'h00; else counter <= counter + 8'd1;` update, instead of iteration 1’s unconditional natural-wrap increment. Keep the synchronous active-high reset and registered `pwm_out <= (counter < duty)` behavior unchanged, including sampling the current counter and duty each cycle. Preserve all observable cycles and reset behavior; do not add a numeric latency annotation.
